subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should Control UI browser Talk start from implicit realtime credential availability, or only after an explicit talk.catalog/talk.realtime readiness preflight says realtime voice is usable?
rationale: Current code and docs treat browser Talk as a realtime surface that can be enabled by OpenAI API-key/OAuth/Codex auth, while this report expects local/non-Realtime Talk setup not to start OpenAI WebRTC; either direction changes user-facing setup semantics.

options.title: Gate on Gateway readiness
options.body: Use talk.catalog realtime.ready to disable or block Talk before microphone startup and show a specific setup message while preserving the chosen credential policy.

options.title: Keep implicit credential activation
options.body: Accept that configured OpenAI realtime credentials enable browser Talk and narrow remaining work to clearer provider/API error messages.

options.title: Require explicit realtime config
options.body: Only show or start browser Talk when talk.realtime is explicitly configured, with upgrade communication for users relying on implicit credentials.

recommendation.title: Gate on Gateway readiness
recommendation.body: Use talk.catalog realtime.ready to disable or block Talk before microphone startup and show a specific setup message while preserving the chosen credential policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent merged OpenAI Realtime auth/docs work and live proof came from steipete, making this the closest current owner trail for the enablement policy choice.
